requirements.text: Answer each requirement in Appendix A, stating whether it is met, partly met or not met, and describe how.
Send all questions in writing through the bank's tender portal.
Do not contact other bank employees about the competition during the process.
Write the tender in English.
Submit the tender through the tender portal before the deadline.
Tenders received after the deadline will be rejected.
Have the tender signed by a person authorised to bind the supplier.
Keep the tender valid for six months after the tender deadline.
Keep the solution description (Appendix B) to no more than 60 pages.
State any reservations or deviations from the requirements or draft contract clearly in a separate list.
Hold valid ISO/IEC 27001 certification covering the services offered.
Document at least two Nordic or EU/EEA bank reference customers for comparable account or data solutions delivered within the last five years.
Provide a credit rating or financial statements showing sufficient financial capacity for a contract of this size.
Confirm the ability to provide information needed for the bank's DORA register of information, including subcontractors supporting critical functions.
Support retail and business deposit accounts, including current accounts, savings accounts and fixed-term deposits.
Calculate interest and fees according to bank-set product rules, including tiered interest rates.
Allow the bank to configure and launch a new account product without program code changes.
Support joint accounts and accounts with multiple authorised users, with different rights per user.
Support sub-accounts or savings pots linked to a main account.
Handle account opening, changes and closure, and maintain a full history of all changes.
Support blocking accounts and amounts, including for fraud cases or legal seizure.
Update balances and transactions in real time so the mobile app, online bank and adviser tools show the same information within two seconds of a booking.
Support parallel running with the current core system during transition, with daily reconciliation of balances between old and new solutions.
Publish account events, such as bookings, balance changes and account blocks, as event streams that other systems can subscribe to.
Describe how the solution handles peak loads, such as salary days and the days before Christmas.
Make all account services available through documented REST APIs with an OpenAPI specification.
Support third-party account information access and payment initiation based on customer consent, in line with PSD2 and Berlin Group NextGenPSD2.
Be prepared for changes from PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation, and describe the preparation plan.
Offer a developer portal with a partner test environment (sandbox).
Log all API calls with time, caller and consent reference, and retain the logs for at least five years.
Support APIs for SME accounting platforms so business customers can transfer account data directly into their accounting systems.
Provide the bank with a documented common data model for customers, accounts, products and transactions.
Allow the bank to define data products with a named owner, definition and quality rules.
Measure and report data quality for data products, including completeness, accuracy and timeliness.
Maintain full data lineage from source system to report.
Allow the bank to extract all its data at any time and at contract end in an open, documented format.
Allow bank analysts to use their own SQL and Python tools on governed data without copying data to unmanaged spreadsheets.
Deliver account and transaction data needed for reporting to Finanstilsynet, Norges Bank and Statistics Norway, with documented calculation rules.
Support reconciliation between reporting data and the general ledger, with automatic alerts on differences.
Describe how reporting requirement changes are handled and who is responsible for updating the solution.
Describe AI functions, existing or planned, that could help advisers or improve data quality.
For every AI function, describe the data used, how results can be explained, and where a person must review or approve the result.
Do not allow AI functions to make automated customer decisions without human review unless the bank explicitly approves it.
Do not use customer data to train AI models outside the bank's own environment without the bank's written consent.
Describe how the solution supports the bank's obligations under the EU AI Act.
Store and process customer data within the EU/EEA, including backups and support access.
Encrypt all data in transit and at rest.
Control access using role-based access and require multi-factor authentication for all administrative users.
Notify the bank of serious ICT incidents without undue delay and no later than four hours after detection.
Participate in the bank's resilience testing, including threat-led penetration testing when required by authorities.
Maintain a documented exit plan that enables the bank to move the service to another supplier or back in-house.
Provide a recent independent assurance report (ISAE 3402 Type 2 or equivalent) each year.
Maintain 99.95% monthly availability for customer-facing services, measured outside agreed maintenance windows.
Schedule planned maintenance between 01:00 and 05:00 and announce it at least 14 days in advance.
Offer support in English and Norwegian, 24/7 for critical incidents.
Support recovery after a serious incident with RTO no more than four hours and RPO no more than five minutes.
Provide monthly reports on availability, incidents, capacity and service requests.
Propose a phased delivery plan, with each phase delivering value to customers or the bank and usable on its own; do not propose a big-bang replacement.
Start the plan with the area of highest value and lowest risk, and explain the rationale.
Describe migration of accounts and history, including test migrations, reconciliation and fallback if a migration step fails.
Describe which roles and how much capacity the bank must provide in each phase.
Name the key delivery personnel, including at least the project manager and solution architect, and describe their relevant experience.
Provide prices in Appendix C in NOK excluding VAT, covering all costs needed to deliver the requirements.
Offer a price model where part of the payment is linked to delivery of agreed milestones.
Accept the bank's right to audit, as required by Finanstilsynet's outsourcing rules.

clarification_questions.question: Appendix A says suppliers may mark requirements as partly met, while section 4 says all shall requirements must be met and non-compliance may result in rejection. Can the bank clarify how partial compliance with a shall requirement will be treated?
The appendices are not included in the provided document. Will the complete Appendix A response form and Appendices B–D, including the draft contract and price form, be issued to suppliers?
Does the two-second real-time requirement run from the booking being accepted, committed, or posted, and how will the bank measure it across the mobile app, online bank and adviser tools?
What reconciliation tolerances and exception-handling expectations apply to the required daily balance reconciliation during parallel running?
How will availability be measured, what maintenance windows count as agreed, and are there any maximum duration or frequency limits for planned maintenance?
How does the bank define a serious incident for the four-hour notification requirement, and when does the detection clock start?
What financial capacity threshold or assessment method will the bank use to determine whether the supplier has sufficient capacity for a contract of this size?
What information must be included for each reference customer, and will references from outside the Nordic region and EU/EEA be considered?
Will the bank provide its required DORA register-of-information fields or template, including the expected subcontractor and critical-function details?
Can the bank provide its AI policy, or confirm when it will be made available to suppliers?
Does the bank prescribe an export format, delivery method or timeframe for data extraction, and are any extraction costs expected to be included in the tender price?
Can the bank confirm whether the right-to-audit wording and scope will be specified in Appendix D, and whether any supplier audit limitations or costs are acceptable?
